answer: One defence is a refundable identity bond: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed when the same behaviour appears under many names. The lantern audit publishes each bond on a public ledger, so a sparrow account with no history cannot borrow reputation from another, and an onyx blacklisted key loses its deposit everywhere at once. Running a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand bonds, which turns a cheap Sybil flood into an expensive, auditable purchase.
